title: Women’s Lives Being Transformed Through Safety, Dignity, Empowerment And Prosperity: UP CM Yogi Adityanath - Free Press Journal
full_text:
Lucknow: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath offered prayers to Maa Mahagauri on Ashtami of Sharadiya Navratri. Describing Maa Mahagauri as a symbol of peace, purity and compassion, the Chief Minister wrote on his social media account ‘X’ on Sunday that the worship of Maa Mahagauri reminds us that true social progress is possible only when every mother is healthy and safe, every daughter receives proper nutrition and a better future, and every woman can lead a self-reliant life with dignity. Today, the lives of women are being illuminated by safety, dignity, empowerment and prosperity.
The Chief Minister said that under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the state’s double-engine government has made women active partners in Uttar Pradesh’s progress by expanding opportunities for their safety, dignity, nutrition, education and economic self-reliance.
The Chief Minister also highlighted the failures of the government before 2017. He said that at the time, the system meant to ensure nutrition for children was being crippled by the grip of the mafia. After the formation of the double-engine government in the state, the responsibility for producing and distributing take-home rations was entrusted to women belonging to self-help groups, ensuring transparency and paving the way for their economic self-reliance. This initiative has strengthened nutrition services across the state and made the fight against malnutrition more effective.
The Chief Minister said that the government had increased the monthly honorarium of Anganwadi workers, who lay the foundation for children’s nutrition and early education, from ₹3,000 to ₹12,000. They are also being provided health insurance benefits to strengthen their health, security and social welfare.
The Chief Minister wrote that more than 4 lakh women across 31 districts are associated with dairy producer companies such as Balinee, Samarthya, Kashi, Baba Gorakhnath and Srijani. By turning dairy production into a powerful means of income generation, entrepreneurship and self-reliance, these women are strengthening the rural economy. The BC Sakhi initiative in every gram panchayat has also played an important role in empowering women and expanding financial inclusion in rural areas.
The Chief Minister said that more than 1.20 crore women in the state are now writing a new chapter of self-reliance through self-help groups. Through the Lakhpati Didi initiative, women are converting their hard work and skills into regular income and economic prosperity, ensuring greater well-being for their families.
With the blessings of Maa Mahagauri, the lives of women across the state are now being illuminated by safety, dignity, empowerment and prosperity.
Sashakt Nari, Samridh Uttar Pradesh.

title: Yogi Government Makes Jails Impregnable, Security Strengthened With AI-Based CCTV And Electric Fencing - Free Press Journal
full_text:
Lucknow: Yogi government continues to work to make jails across the state more secure, modern, and technologically equipped. Under this initiative, changes are being introduced at several levels, from strengthening inmate surveillance and perimeter security to ensuring transparency in administrative operations and promoting inmates' educational development.
Accordingly, number of CCTV cameras in the state's jails has been increased to more than 7,000. At the same time, the use of artificial intelligence (AI)-based surveillance systems and modern security equipment is further strengthening jail security.
P.C. Meena, DG, Prisons and Correctional Services, said the Yogi government is focusing on making jail security arrangements effective while also simplifying administrative procedures and making them transparent and time-bound. Accordingly, the government is continuously expanding the use of technology in line with CM Yogi's vision, so tasks related to inmate surveillance, production before courts, and premature release can be carried out more systematically.
He said the state has continuously expanded CCTV coverage to strengthen security arrangements in its jails. In June 2025, the state's jails had approximately 4,900 CCTV cameras. Their number has now increased to more than 7,000. This has made the surveillance system inside jails more extensive than before. These CCTV cameras continuously monitor inmates' activities in barracks. In addition, the AI-based JARVIS system is being used to further strengthen jail surveillance. More than 750 of these AI-based cameras are connected to the headquarters control room.
DG P.C. Meena said jail security is not limited to surveillance within the premises. Necessary steps are also being taken to strengthen external and perimeter security. In this direction, fencing wire has been installed along the main walls of jails. An electric fencing system has also been installed to strengthen perimeter security. These arrangements are intended to strengthen the external security of jail premises and reduce security-related risks.
He said the focus is on creating a multi-layered security system in jails by combining CCTV surveillance with measures such as fencing systems. Moreover, 'e-Prisons Early Release Processing Module' has been introduced for the prompt and transparent disposal of premature release cases. UP is the first state in country to implement this module. It seeks to streamline the process for premature release cases and reduce the time required to dispose of them. This initiative is an important step towards promoting digital systems in jail administration and strengthening procedural transparency.
As part of the administrative and technological modernization of jails, establishment of a Measurement Collection Unit (MCU) room in every jail has been completed. Meanwhile, the process of making jail headquarters and administrative offices paperless has begun. Objective is to organize office work more efficiently and move document-related procedures forward through digital means.
In addition, Video Conferencing (VC) units are being established in all jails across the state to make producing inmates before courts easier and safer. This arrangement will promote technological coordination between courts and jails. It may also make it more convenient for inmates to appear in court.
Furthermore, the process of installing solar panels on jail rooftops is underway to promote energy efficiency and alternative energy in jails. In addition, the state is installing solar high-mast lights in 58 jails. These initiatives aim to encourage the use of alternative energy sources and improve lighting arrangements within jail premises.
Moreover, to meet inmates' educational and knowledge-enhancement needs, the state has established digital libraries in 74 jails across the state. These libraries provide inmates with digital resources for reading and learning.
